Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
WMU 108 Deer and Elk Survey – February 2018 
 
Background 
WMU 108 is typically flown every 3 years in the Aerial Ungulate survey rotation. It is managed for trophy mule 
deer and is a desirable zone for hunters not only from Lethbridge but from across the province. It has been 
surveyed using the Gasaway survey method in 2008 and in 2011 and previous to that us ing a stratified trend 
survey.  
 
Due to the desire to survey for multiple species and have systematic representative coverage of all areas, WMU 
108 was surveyed using a transect survey method this year (winter of 2017/18). This report provides results of the 
survey conducted by Alberta Environment and Parks in February 2018. 
Survey method 
Surveys were flown in a Bell 206B from February 9 to 11, 2018. 400 metres wide east-west transects spaced 1 
min in latitude were flown for the entire WMU providing equal coverage of all habitat types throu ghout the WMU.  
 
Observers counted all mule deer and white-tailed deer within 200 metres of each side of the aircraft. Elk were 
seen and recorded for the entire distance between flight lines (approximately 950  metres on either side of the 
aircraft) providing a census count for elk. For mule deer and white-tailed deer, a density was calculated within the 
transect based on number of deer observed and applied to the area of the entire WMU for an acceptable 
population estimate. For elk, the total number of elk seen during the entire survey becomes the population 
estimate. 
Results 
The total area of survey effort was 994.33 km 2. A total of 2088 mule deer were observed and recorded and a total 
of 1167 white-tailed deer were observed and recorded. This indicated a density of 2.10 mule deer per km2 and 
1.17 white-tailed deer per km2. The area of the entire WMU 108 is 4519.5 km. This provides a population estimate 
of 9490 mule deer and 5304 white-tailed deer. 
 
198 elk were observed over the entire survey and it is assumed all were observed for a complete count of elk in 
WMU 108.
